dialogue.text: in all of Russian history.

dialogue.ja: ロシアの歴史全体で。
dialogue.local: in all of Russian history.
dialogue.en: in all of Russian history.

dialogue.local: He signed the abdication document and requested permission to depart from Russia.
dialogue.en: He signed the abdication document and requested permission to depart from Russia.

dialogue.text: St. Petersburg, winter 1762.

dialogue.ja: サンクトペテルブルク、1762年冬。
dialogue.local: St. Petersburg, winter 1762.
dialogue.en: St. Petersburg, winter 1762.

dialogue.text: Catherine was now Serena of Russia, but her rain was far from secure.
dialogue.zh: Catherine was now Serena of Russia, but her rain was far from secure.
dialogue.ja: カトリナは今やロシアの女帝だったが、その統治は決して安定していなかった。
dialogue.local: Catherine was now Serena of Russia, but her rain was far from secure.
dialogue.en: Catherine was now Serena of Russia, but her rain was far from secure.

dialogue.text: The coup had succeeded, but the plotting and scheming had only just begun.
dialogue.zh: The coup had succeeded, but the plotting and scheming had only just begun.
dialogue.ja: クーデターは成功したが、陰謀と策略は始まったばかりだった。
dialogue.local: The coup had succeeded, but the plotting and scheming had only just begun.
dialogue.en: The coup had succeeded, but the plotting and scheming had only just begun.

dialogue.text: The old networks of her murdered husband were forming at court, influential nobles,
dialogue.zh: The old networks of her murdered husband were forming at court, influential nobles,
dialogue.ja: 殺された夫の古い勢力が宮廷で形成されつつあり、影響力のある貴族たち、
dialogue.local: The old networks of her murdered husband were forming at court, influential nobles,
dialogue.en: The old networks of her murdered husband were forming at court, influential nobles,

dialogue.text: generals, court officials.
dialogue.zh: generals, court officials.
dialogue.ja: 将軍、宮廷役人。
dialogue.local: generals, court officials.
dialogue.en: generals, court officials.

dialogue.text: She doubted her legitimacy.
dialogue.zh: She doubted her legitimacy.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は自分の正当性を疑った。
dialogue.local: She doubted her legitimacy.
dialogue.en: She doubted her legitimacy.

dialogue.text: Catherine stood utterly alone as a German princess on the Russian imperial throne.
dialogue.zh: Catherine stood utterly alone as a German princess on the Russian imperial throne.
dialogue.ja: カタリナはドイツの王女として、ロシア帝国の玉座に完全に一人で立っていた。
dialogue.local: Catherine stood utterly alone as a German princess on the Russian imperial throne.
dialogue.en: Catherine stood utterly alone as a German princess on the Russian imperial throne.

dialogue.text: With clever tact, political instinct and ice-cold calculation, she began to secure power.
dialogue.zh: With clever tact, political instinct and ice-cold calculation, she began to secure power.
dialogue.ja: 巧みな策略、政治的本能、冷徹な計算で、彼女は権力を確立し始めた。
dialogue.local: With clever tact, political instinct and ice-cold calculation, she began to secure power.
dialogue.en: With clever tact, political instinct and ice-cold calculation, she began to secure power.

dialogue.text: She rewarded, threatened, negotiated.
dialogue.zh: She rewarded, threatened, negotiated.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は報酬を与え、脅し、交渉した。
dialogue.local: She rewarded, threatened, negotiated.
dialogue.en: She rewarded, threatened, negotiated.

dialogue.text: She was no dreamer but a strategist, and she was aware of the greatest threat to her rule.
dialogue.zh: She was no dreamer but a strategist, and she was aware of the greatest threat to her rule.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は夢想家ではなく戦略家であり、自分の支配に対する最大の脅威を認識していた。
dialogue.local: She was no dreamer but a strategist, and she was aware of the greatest threat to her rule.
dialogue.en: She was no dreamer but a strategist, and she was aware of the greatest threat to her rule.

dialogue.text: Ive N. VI.
dialogue.zh: Ive N. VI.
dialogue.ja: イヴ6世。
dialogue.local: Ive N. VI.
dialogue.en: Ive N. VI.

dialogue.zh: The former child emperor was still alive, imprisoned in the Schlisselberg fortress.
dialogue.ja: かつての子供皇帝はまだ生きており、シュリッセルベルク要塞に囚われていた。
dialogue.local: The former child emperor was still alive, imprisoned in the Schlisselberg fortress.
dialogue.en: The former child emperor was still alive, imprisoned in the Schlisselberg fortress.

dialogue.text: He was the final legitimate czar and a perfect instrument for any adversary who sought
dialogue.zh: He was the final legitimate czar and a perfect instrument for any adversary who sought
dialogue.ja: 彼は最後の正当なツァーリであり、敵対者にとって完璧な道具だった。
dialogue.local: He was the final legitimate czar and a perfect instrument for any adversary who sought
dialogue.en: He was the final legitimate czar and a perfect instrument for any adversary who sought

dialogue.text: to clip Catherine's wings.
dialogue.zh: to clip Catherine's wings.
dialogue.ja: カタリナの翼を切り落とすための。
dialogue.local: to clip Catherine's wings.
dialogue.en: to clip Catherine's wings.

dialogue.text: For over 20 years, he had been kept hidden.
dialogue.zh: For over 20 years, he had been kept hidden.
dialogue.ja: 20年以上も隠されていた。
dialogue.local: For over 20 years, he had been kept hidden.
dialogue.en: For over 20 years, he had been kept hidden.

dialogue.text: Catherine decided to see him with her own eyes.
dialogue.zh: Catherine decided to see him with her own eyes.
dialogue.ja: カタリナは自分の目で彼を見ることに決めた。
dialogue.local: Catherine decided to see him with her own eyes.
dialogue.en: Catherine decided to see him with her own eyes.

dialogue.text: Schlisselberg 1764.
dialogue.zh: Schlisselberg 1764.
dialogue.ja: シュリッセルベルク、1764年。
dialogue.local: Schlisselberg 1764.
dialogue.en: Schlisselberg 1764.

dialogue.text: The czarina entered the gloomy fortress and what she saw there made her shudder.
dialogue.zh: The czarina entered the gloomy fortress and what she saw there made her shudder.
dialogue.ja: 女帝は陰鬱な要塞に入り、そこで見たものに震え上がった。
dialogue.local: The czarina entered the gloomy fortress and what she saw there made her shudder.
dialogue.en: The czarina entered the gloomy fortress and what she saw there made her shudder.

dialogue.text: Catherine was neither a madman nor a broken man.
dialogue.zh: Catherine was neither a madman nor a broken man.
dialogue.ja: カタリナは狂人でも壊れた人間でもなかった。
dialogue.local: Catherine was neither a madman nor a broken man.
dialogue.en: Catherine was neither a madman nor a broken man.

dialogue.text: He was perfectly lucid and he recognized her instantly and without a doubt.
dialogue.zh: He was perfectly lucid and he recognized her instantly and without a doubt.
dialogue.ja: 彼は完全に正気で、彼女を即座に疑いなく認識しました。
dialogue.local: He was perfectly lucid and he recognized her instantly and without a doubt.
dialogue.en: He was perfectly lucid and he recognized her instantly and without a doubt.

dialogue.text: He didn't speak often, but he knew exactly who he was and that he was the legitimate ruler.
dialogue.zh: He didn't speak often, but he knew exactly who he was and that he was the legitimate ruler.
dialogue.ja: 彼はあまり話さなかったが、自分が誰であるか、正当な支配者であることを正確に知っていました。
dialogue.local: He didn't speak often, but he knew exactly who he was and that he was the legitimate ruler.
dialogue.en: He didn't speak often, but he knew exactly who he was and that he was the legitimate ruler.

dialogue.text: Catherine left the fortress and the decision had been made secretly, quietly, without public
dialogue.zh: Catherine left the fortress and the decision had been made secretly, quietly, without public
dialogue.ja: エカチェリーナは要塞を離れ、その決定は秘密裏に、静かに、公にされることなく行われました。
dialogue.local: Catherine left the fortress and the decision had been made secretly, quietly, without public
dialogue.en: Catherine left the fortress and the decision had been made secretly, quietly, without public

dialogue.text: spectacle.
dialogue.zh: spectacle.
dialogue.ja: 見世物として。
dialogue.local: spectacle.
dialogue.en: spectacle.

dialogue.text: His grave remains unknown to this day.
dialogue.zh: His grave remains unknown to this day.
dialogue.ja: 彼の墓は今日まで不明のままです。
dialogue.local: His grave remains unknown to this day.
dialogue.en: His grave remains unknown to this day.

dialogue.text: Gregory Orlov, soldier, daredevil, hero of the coup.
dialogue.zh: Gregory Orlov, soldier, daredevil, hero of the coup.
dialogue.ja: グレゴリー・オルロフ、兵士、冒険家、クーデターの英雄。
dialogue.local: Gregory Orlov, soldier, daredevil, hero of the coup.
dialogue.en: Gregory Orlov, soldier, daredevil, hero of the coup.

dialogue.text: He had helped Catherine gain power and she had loved him.
dialogue.zh: He had helped Catherine gain power and she had loved him.
dialogue.ja: 彼はエカチェリーナが権力を得るのを助け、彼女は彼を愛していました。
dialogue.local: He had helped Catherine gain power and she had loved him.
dialogue.en: He had helped Catherine gain power and she had loved him.

dialogue.text: But over the years, the relationship became a burden.
dialogue.zh: But over the years, the relationship became a burden.
dialogue.ja: しかし、年月が経つにつれて、その関係は重荷となりました。
dialogue.local: But over the years, the relationship became a burden.
dialogue.en: But over the years, the relationship became a burden.

dialogue.text: As early as 1762, she had a son, a Lexay.
dialogue.zh: As early as 1762, she had a son, a Lexay.
dialogue.ja: 1762年にはすでに息子のレクサイがいました。
dialogue.local: As early as 1762, she had a son, a Lexay.
dialogue.en: As early as 1762, she had a son, a Lexay.

dialogue.text: But not even the bond of their shared child held them together anymore.
dialogue.zh: But not even the bond of their shared child held them together anymore.
dialogue.ja: しかし、共有する子供の絆さえも彼らを結びつけることはできませんでした。
dialogue.local: But not even the bond of their shared child held them together anymore.
dialogue.en: But not even the bond of their shared child held them together anymore.

dialogue.text: She was just waiting for the right moment to break free.
dialogue.zh: She was just waiting for the right moment to break free.
dialogue.ja: 彼女はただ解放される適切な瞬間を待っていただけでした。
dialogue.local: She was just waiting for the right moment to break free.
dialogue.en: She was just waiting for the right moment to break free.

dialogue.text: Then came Potemkin, Gregory Alexander-Vitch, a guards officer, clever, well-read, charming.
dialogue.zh: Then came Potemkin, Gregory Alexander-Vitch, a guards officer, clever, well-read, charming.
dialogue.ja: そしてポチョムキン、グレゴリー・アレクサンドルヴィッチが現れました。彼は警備隊の士官で、賢く、博識で魅力的でした。
dialogue.local: Then came Potemkin, Gregory Alexander-Vitch, a guards officer, clever, well-read, charming.
dialogue.en: Then came Potemkin, Gregory Alexander-Vitch, a guards officer, clever, well-read, charming.

dialogue.text: People talked amongst themselves and there were quiet whispers circulating all throughout
dialogue.zh: People talked amongst themselves and there were quiet whispers circulating all throughout
dialogue.ja: 人々はひそひそ話を交わし、宮殿中に静かなささやきが広がっていました。
dialogue.local: People talked amongst themselves and there were quiet whispers circulating all throughout
dialogue.en: People talked amongst themselves and there were quiet whispers circulating all throughout

dialogue.text: the palace.
dialogue.zh: the palace.
dialogue.ja: 宮殿中に。
dialogue.local: the palace.
dialogue.en: the palace.

dialogue.text: A formal public ceremony was completely out of the question.
dialogue.zh: A formal public ceremony was completely out of the question.
dialogue.ja: 正式な公開式典は全く問題外でした。
dialogue.local: A formal public ceremony was completely out of the question.
dialogue.en: A formal public ceremony was completely out of the question.

dialogue.text: It simply could not be considered.
dialogue.zh: It simply could not be considered.
dialogue.ja: それは単純に考慮されることはありませんでした。
dialogue.local: It simply could not be considered.
dialogue.en: It simply could not be considered.

dialogue.text: She would have had to share her power and Catherine didn't do that with anyone.
dialogue.zh: She would have had to share her power and Catherine didn't do that with anyone.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は権力を分かち合わなければならなかったが、エカチェリーナは誰ともそうしませんでした。
dialogue.local: She would have had to share her power and Catherine didn't do that with anyone.
dialogue.en: She would have had to share her power and Catherine didn't do that with anyone.

dialogue.text: What they did share with each other, however, was unique.
dialogue.zh: What they did share with each other, however, was unique.
dialogue.ja: しかし、彼らが互いに共有したものは独特でした。
dialogue.local: What they did share with each other, however, was unique.
dialogue.en: What they did share with each other, however, was unique.

dialogue.text: It was a deeply passionate connection that manifested itself both in intensely physical
dialogue.zh: It was a deeply passionate connection that manifested itself both in intensely physical
dialogue.ja: それは深く情熱的なつながりで、強烈な身体的側面にも現れていました。
dialogue.local: It was a deeply passionate connection that manifested itself both in intensely physical
dialogue.en: It was a deeply passionate connection that manifested itself both in intensely physical

dialogue.text: and profoundly political ways.
dialogue.zh: and profoundly political ways.
dialogue.ja: そして深く政治的な形でも表れていました。
dialogue.local: and profoundly political ways.
dialogue.en: and profoundly political ways.

dialogue.text: 1,775 Catherine gave birth to a daughter, Elisavetta, Potemkin's child.
dialogue.zh: 1,775 Catherine gave birth to a daughter, Elisavetta, Potemkin's child.
dialogue.ja: 1775年、エカチェリーナは娘エリサヴェッタを出産しました。ポチョムキンの子供です。
dialogue.local: 1,775 Catherine gave birth to a daughter, Elisavetta, Potemkin's child.
dialogue.en: 1,775 Catherine gave birth to a daughter, Elisavetta, Potemkin's child.

dialogue.text: But the public learned nothing of it.
dialogue.zh: But the public learned nothing of it.
dialogue.ja: しかし、公には何も知らされませんでした。
dialogue.local: But the public learned nothing of it.
dialogue.en: But the public learned nothing of it.

dialogue.text: The young girl grew up hidden under the protection of the Empress.
dialogue.zh: The young girl grew up hidden under the protection of the Empress.
dialogue.ja: その若い少女は女帝の保護のもとで隠れて育ちました。
dialogue.local: The young girl grew up hidden under the protection of the Empress.
dialogue.en: The young girl grew up hidden under the protection of the Empress.

dialogue.text: Catherine knew, to be a great power, you must move borders.
dialogue.zh: Catherine knew, to be a great power, you must move borders.
dialogue.ja: エカチェリーナは、偉大な権力になるには国境を動かさなければならないと知っていました。
dialogue.local: Catherine knew, to be a great power, you must move borders.
dialogue.en: Catherine knew, to be a great power, you must move borders.

dialogue.text: As our Peter the Great fought for Russia's access to the Baltic Sea, now Catherine wanted
dialogue.zh: As our Peter the Great fought for Russia's access to the Baltic Sea, now Catherine wanted
dialogue.ja: 私たちのピョートル大帝がロシアのバルト海へのアクセスのために戦ったように、今やエカチェリーナは
dialogue.local: As our Peter the Great fought for Russia's access to the Baltic Sea, now Catherine wanted
dialogue.en: As our Peter the Great fought for Russia's access to the Baltic Sea, now Catherine wanted

dialogue.text: to conquer the south, the Black Sea, the Crimea, maybe even Constantinople.
dialogue.zh: to conquer the south, the Black Sea, the Crimea, maybe even Constantinople.
dialogue.ja: 南方、黒海、クリミア、そしておそらくコンスタンティノープルを征服したいと思っていました。
dialogue.local: to conquer the south, the Black Sea, the Crimea, maybe even Constantinople.
dialogue.en: to conquer the south, the Black Sea, the Crimea, maybe even Constantinople.

dialogue.text: In 1768, the Ottoman Empire declared war on Russia.
dialogue.zh: In 1768, the Ottoman Empire declared war on Russia.
dialogue.ja: 1768年、オスマン帝国はロシアに宣戦布告しました。
dialogue.local: In 1768, the Ottoman Empire declared war on Russia.
dialogue.en: In 1768, the Ottoman Empire declared war on Russia.

dialogue.text: Catherine forged alliances, practiced diplomacy, and dispatched her troops.
dialogue.zh: Catherine forged alliances, practiced diplomacy, and dispatched her troops.
dialogue.ja: エカチェリーナは同盟を結び、外交を行い、軍隊を派遣しました。
dialogue.local: Catherine forged alliances, practiced diplomacy, and dispatched her troops.
dialogue.en: Catherine forged alliances, practiced diplomacy, and dispatched her troops.

dialogue.text: Gregory Orloth and later Potemkin took command.

dialogue.local: Gregory Orloth and later Potemkin took command.
dialogue.en: Gregory Orloth and later Potemkin took command.

dialogue.text: For Catherine, it was more than just a military campaign.
dialogue.zh: For Catherine, it was more than just a military campaign.
dialogue.ja: エカチェリーナにとって、それは単なる軍事作戦以上のものでした。
dialogue.local: For Catherine, it was more than just a military campaign.
dialogue.en: For Catherine, it was more than just a military campaign.

dialogue.text: The plan was bold, occupied the Crimea, pushed back Ottoman influence, and create a new
dialogue.zh: The plan was bold, occupied the Crimea, pushed back Ottoman influence, and create a new

dialogue.local: The plan was bold, occupied the Crimea, pushed back Ottoman influence, and create a new
dialogue.en: The plan was bold, occupied the Crimea, pushed back Ottoman influence, and create a new

dialogue.text: Russia.
dialogue.zh: Russia.
dialogue.ja: ロシアを作り出すことでした。
dialogue.local: Russia.
dialogue.en: Russia.

dialogue.text: A flourishing province in the south.
dialogue.zh: A flourishing province in the south.
dialogue.ja: 南部の繁栄する州。
dialogue.local: A flourishing province in the south.
dialogue.en: A flourishing province in the south.

dialogue.text: A shadow fell over the Tsar's empire, not from the west, but from within its own land.
dialogue.zh: A shadow fell over the Tsar's empire, not from the west, but from within its own land.
dialogue.ja: ツァーリの帝国に影が落ちました。それは西からではなく、自国の中からでした。
dialogue.local: A shadow fell over the Tsar's empire, not from the west, but from within its own land.
dialogue.en: A shadow fell over the Tsar's empire, not from the west, but from within its own land.

dialogue.text: In 1773, along the Volga, the people rose up.
dialogue.zh: In 1773, along the Volga, the people rose up.
dialogue.ja: 1773年、ヴォルガ川沿いで人々が蜂起しました。
dialogue.local: In 1773, along the Volga, the people rose up.
dialogue.en: In 1773, along the Volga, the people rose up.

dialogue.zh: Emilian Pugachev, a casa, declared himself to be Tsar Peter III.
dialogue.ja: エミリアン・プガチョフという農民が自らをツァーリ・ピョートル3世と宣言しました。
dialogue.local: Emilian Pugachev, a casa, declared himself to be Tsar Peter III.
dialogue.en: Emilian Pugachev, a casa, declared himself to be Tsar Peter III.

dialogue.text: The uprising became the greatest revolt in Russian history until the revolution of 1917.
dialogue.zh: The uprising became the greatest revolt in Russian history until the revolution of 1917.
dialogue.ja: この蜂起は1917年の革命までロシア史上最大の反乱となりました。
dialogue.local: The uprising became the greatest revolt in Russian history until the revolution of 1917.
dialogue.en: The uprising became the greatest revolt in Russian history until the revolution of 1917.

dialogue.text: Surfkossacks, peasants, religious minorities, they all followed the false Tsar.
dialogue.zh: Surfkossacks, peasants, religious minorities, they all followed the false Tsar.
dialogue.ja: コサック、農民、宗教的少数派が皆偽のツァーリに従いました。
dialogue.local: Surfkossacks, peasants, religious minorities, they all followed the false Tsar.
dialogue.en: Surfkossacks, peasants, religious minorities, they all followed the false Tsar.

dialogue.text: A war from below against the system, against the nobility, against the Tsars.
dialogue.zh: A war from below against the system, against the nobility, against the Tsars.
dialogue.ja: 体制、貴族、ツァーリに対する下からの戦争でした。
dialogue.local: A war from below against the system, against the nobility, against the Tsars.
dialogue.en: A war from below against the system, against the nobility, against the Tsars.

dialogue.text: Catherine was shaken.
dialogue.zh: Catherine was shaken.
dialogue.ja: エカチェリーナは動揺しました。
dialogue.local: Catherine was shaken.
dialogue.en: Catherine was shaken.

dialogue.text: The nightmare she had dreaded more than anything else had now truly become a reality.
dialogue.zh: The nightmare she had dreaded more than anything else had now truly become a reality.
dialogue.ja: 彼女が何よりも恐れていた悪夢が今や本当に現実となりました。

dialogue.en: The nightmare she had dreaded more than anything else had now truly become a reality.

dialogue.en: her reign itself.

dialogue.zh: While Europe was in a state of upheaval, Catherine received a message that changed everything.
dialogue.ja: ヨーロッパが動乱の状態にある中、エカチェリーナはすべてを変えるメッセージを受け取りました。
dialogue.local: While Europe was in a state of upheaval, Catherine received a message that changed everything.
dialogue.en: While Europe was in a state of upheaval, Catherine received a message that changed everything.

dialogue.zh: Gregory Potemkin, who was her closest confidant and her one great love, was on his deathbed.
dialogue.ja: 彼女の最も親しい信頼者であり、唯一の大きな愛であったグレゴリー・ポチョムキンが臨終にありました。
dialogue.local: Gregory Potemkin, who was her closest confidant and her one great love, was on his deathbed.
dialogue.en: Gregory Potemkin, who was her closest confidant and her one great love, was on his deathbed.

dialogue.ja: 彼女は「あなたの健康がとても心配です」と書きました。
dialogue.local: I am terribly worried about your health, she wrote.
dialogue.en: I am terribly worried about your health, she wrote.

dialogue.text: To belong to the state, you belong to me.

dialogue.ja: 国家に属するなら、あなたは私に属します。
dialogue.local: To belong to the state, you belong to me.
dialogue.en: To belong to the state, you belong to me.

dialogue.en: With him, she lost not only a man, but the only person who understood her both as a woman

dialogue.text: and a ruler.

dialogue.ja: そして支配者としても彼女を理解する唯一の人物を失いました。
dialogue.local: and a ruler.
dialogue.en: and a ruler.

dialogue.text: His finest quality was courage, of the heart and of the mind, she wrote.

dialogue.ja: 彼の最も優れた資質は心と精神の勇気でした、と彼女は書きました。

dialogue.en: alliance, and a turning point for Catherine.

dialogue.en: From then on, she was alone.

dialogue.en: was something else.

dialogue.text: Her son, Paul, the heir to the throne whom she never loved, whom she never trusted.
dialogue.zh: Her son, Paul, the heir to the throne whom she never loved, whom she never trusted.
dialogue.ja: 彼女の息子ポール、王位継承者でありながら、彼女は決して愛さず、信頼もしませんでした。
dialogue.local: Her son, Paul, the heir to the throne whom she never loved, whom she never trusted.
dialogue.en: Her son, Paul, the heir to the throne whom she never loved, whom she never trusted.

dialogue.text: And he was now set to assume her legacy.
dialogue.zh: And he was now set to assume her legacy.

dialogue.en: And he was now set to assume her legacy.

dialogue.text: She feared that he would destroy everything, that he could lead Russia back into darkness,
dialogue.zh: She feared that he would destroy everything, that he could lead Russia back into darkness,
dialogue.ja: 彼女は彼がすべてを破壊し、ロシアを再び暗黒に導くのではないかと恐れていました。

dialogue.en: What remains of her is encapsulated in her own epitaph.

dialogue.text: She wanted to please her husband, the ZARS and the people.
dialogue.zh: She wanted to please her husband, the ZARS and the people.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は夫、ツァーリ、そして民衆を喜ばせたかったのです。
dialogue.local: She wanted to please her husband, the ZARS and the people.
dialogue.en: She wanted to please her husband, the ZARS and the people.

dialogue.text: She read many books.
dialogue.zh: She read many books.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は多くの本を読みました。
dialogue.local: She read many books.
dialogue.en: She read many books.

dialogue.text: She hated no one, had a truly good heart and had friends.
dialogue.zh: She hated no one, had a truly good heart and had friends.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は誰も憎まず、本当に優しい心を持ち、友人もいました。
dialogue.local: She hated no one, had a truly good heart and had friends.
dialogue.en: She hated no one, had a truly good heart and had friends.

dialogue.local: But what became of her children, Katarina gave birth to four children.
dialogue.en: But what became of her children, Katarina gave birth to four children.

dialogue.en: A child who has never allowed to exist politically.

dialogue.en: Elizabetha, born in 1775, the secret daughter of Catherine and Potemkin.

dialogue.ja: 彼女もまた隠されていました。
dialogue.local: She too was kept hidden.
dialogue.en: She too was kept hidden.

dialogue.en: Katarina had her raised in safety, far from the court, and away from the intrigues of power.

dialogue.en: Catherine II, the last great ruler of Europe, between light and shadow.

dialogue.text: And to this day remains one of the most fascinating women in world history.
